breakfast.name: Bolón de Verde (Green Plantain Dumpling)
instructions: Boil or roast green plantains until tender
Mash while still hot — must be smooth and sticky
Mix in crumbled cheese and chicharrón pieces
Shape into large balls — bigger than a baseball
Fry in oil until golden crust forms, or serve as-is (boiled version)
The outside should be crispy, the inside gooey with melted cheese and pork
Serve with a fried egg on top and coffee
This is Ecuador's most important breakfast — coastal Guayaquil runs on bolón
breakfast.description: Ecuador's breakfast powerhouse — a giant ball of mashed green plantain stuffed with cheese and pork cracklings, fried until golden. The cheese-pull when you break it open went viral. Guayaquil wakes up on bolón de verde the way other cities wake up on toast.

breakfast.name: Tigrillo (Smashed Plantain Scramble)
instructions: Boil plantains until tender, mash roughly — keep some chunks
Melt butter, add mashed plantain
Scramble eggs into the plantain, stir together
Add crumbled cheese — it melts through
Season with salt, top with cilantro
Serve with hot sauce and coffee
This is Zaruma's gift to Ecuador — a gold mining town that created the perfect morning fuel
breakfast.description: Smashed green plantain scrambled with eggs and melted cheese — a hearty Ecuadorian breakfast from the gold-mining town of Zaruma. The one-pan technique and the melted-cheese-through-plantain texture make tigrillo a viral Latin American breakfast discovery.

lunch.name: Encebollado (Tuna and Onion Soup)
ingredients: Red onion (sliced into rings, pickled in lime juice)
instructions: Boil yuca until tender but not falling apart
Cook tuna in broth with tomatoes, garlic, cumin
Do not overcook the tuna — it should be tender, not dry
Quick-pickle red onion rings in lime juice and salt
Ladle soup into bowls — yuca and tuna in broth
Top with a mountain of pickled onions
Serve with plantain chips on the side and extra lime
This is Ecuador's hangover cure and national soup — the debate between coast and highlands about the best version is eternal
lunch.description: Ecuador's national soup and world-famous hangover cure — fresh tuna and cassava in a tomato-cumin broth buried under tangy pickled red onions. The most debated dish in Ecuador (every city claims the best version), and the dramatic onion-pile presentation makes it a viral food landmark.

lunch.name: Seco de Chivo (Goat Stew)
ingredients: Naranjilla juice (or orange-lime mix as substitute)
Rice, fried plantain, avocado for serving
instructions: Marinate goat in naranjilla juice and beer overnight
Blend a massive amount of cilantro into a green paste — this is the base color
Sauté onion, garlic, add tomatoes, green pepper, cumin, achiote
Add goat and marinade, bring to simmer
Add cilantro paste — the stew turns bright green
Slow-cook 2+ hours until goat is fall-apart tender
Serve with yellow rice, fried ripe plantain, avocado, and salad
The green color from the cilantro is striking and unusual
lunch.description: Ecuador's celebratory goat stew — braised in naranjilla juice and beer with a shocking amount of cilantro that turns the sauce bright green. The vivid color and fall-apart meat have made seco de chivo a viral Ecuadorian food landmark. Reserved for weekends and celebrations.

dinner.name: Hornado (Whole Roast Pig)
ingredients: 1 whole suckling pig or large pork leg
Marinade: chicha (fermented corn drink) or beer, garlic, cumin, achiote, salt
instructions: Score the skin deeply all over
Marinate in chicha/beer with garlic, cumin, achiote, salt — overnight
Roast in wood-fired oven low and slow for 6+ hours
Baste repeatedly — the skin must become crackly and golden while meat stays moist
The skin should shatter when you tap it — crispy like glass
Carve at the market stall, serve with llapingachos, mote, curtido, and agrio
In Ecuadorian markets, whole hornado sits on display — customers point at which cut they want
The skin-cracking moment is the most viral Ecuadorian food video
dinner.description: Ecuador's market-day centerpiece — whole pig roasted until the skin shatters like glass, served with potato patties and hominy corn. The skin-cracking moment and the market stall carving spectacle are the most filmed food scenes in Ecuador's highlands.

dinner.name: Ceviche de Camarón Ecuatoriano (Shrimp Ceviche)
ingredients: 1kg large shrimp (cooked — not raw, this is Ecuadorian style)
Tomato sauce base: ketchup, orange juice, lime juice, tomato
instructions: Cook shrimp briefly — just until pink, do not overcook
Mix tomato-citrus sauce: ketchup, orange juice, lime juice, diced tomato
Toss shrimp with sauce, soaked red onion, cilantro, chili
Chill — this is served cold
Serve in a glass or bowl with chifles and popcorn on top
Yes, popcorn — this is the Ecuadorian way, and it's genius for crunch
Ecuadorian ceviche uses COOKED shrimp, unlike Peruvian raw ceviche — this is a different tradition
dinner.description: Ecuador's ceviche controversy — cooked shrimp in a tomato-citrus sauce (not raw like Peru's), topped with popcorn and plantain chips. The 'ceviche with ketchup and popcorn' revelation went viral when food creators discovered that Ecuadorian ceviche is an entirely different tradition from Peruvian.

snacks.name: Llapingachos (Stuffed Potato Patties)
ingredients: Peanut sauce: roasted peanuts, milk, onion, achiote
instructions: Mash boiled potatoes smooth
Mix in achiote for golden color
Form into thick patties
Stuff each with a nugget of queso fresco, seal
Pan-fry in oil until golden crust on both sides — cheese melts inside
Make peanut sauce: blend roasted peanuts with milk, sautéed onion, achiote
Serve patties with peanut sauce drizzled over and curtido on side
The cheese-pull when you break one open is the moment
snacks.description: Ecuador's golden potato patties stuffed with cheese — fried until crispy outside with molten cheese inside, served with a creamy peanut sauce. The cheese-pull reveal and the unusual peanut sauce pairing have made llapingachos a viral Ecuadorian street food star.

snacks.name: Empanadas de Viento (Wind Empanadas)
ingredients: Dough: flour, butter, egg, water, salt
Filling: queso fresco (just cheese — nothing else)
instructions: Make simple dough, rest 20 min
Roll out, cut circles
Fill with a generous amount of queso fresco — nothing else goes in
Seal edges, crimp with fork
Deep fry until they puff up dramatically — filled with hot air (hence 'wind')
Dust with sugar while hot
The puffing is dramatic — they inflate like balloons
Bite through the crispy shell to hit the melted cheese inside
The contrast of sweet sugar exterior and salty cheese interior is the hook
snacks.description: Empanadas that inflate like balloons when fried — filled with nothing but cheese and hot air (hence 'de viento' — 'of wind'). Dusted with sugar for a sweet-salty contrast. The dramatic puffing moment is the most satisfying Ecuadorian food video you'll ever see.

desserts.name: Tres Leches Cake (Ecuadorian Style)
ingredients: Cake: 5 eggs, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup flour, vanilla
Three milks: evaporated milk, condensed milk, heavy cream
instructions: Beat eggs and sugar until tripled in volume and pale
Fold in flour gently — do not deflate
Bake at 175°C for 25-30 min until golden and springy
Mix three milks together
Poke holes all over the warm cake
Pour milk mixture over — slowly, letting it absorb fully
Refrigerate at least 4 hours — overnight is better
Top with Italian meringue and torch it, or top with whipped cream
Dust with cinnamon
The cake should be soaked through — moist, not soggy — and the meringue should be dramatic
desserts.description: Ecuador's version of the beloved three-milk cake — sponge soaked in evaporated, condensed, and heavy cream, topped with torched meringue. The 'soaking' video where the milk slowly absorbs into the cake is one of the most satisfying dessert videos on social media across Latin America.

drinks.name: Canelazo (Hot Cinnamon Liquor)
ingredients: Panela (raw cane sugar block) or brown sugar
instructions: Dissolve panela in boiling water with cinnamon sticks and cloves
Simmer 10 min until fragrant and syrupy
Add naranjilla juice
Add aguardiente to taste — be generous, it's cold in the highlands
Serve hot in mugs
This is the Ecuadorian highlands' cold-weather drink — sipped at festivals, markets, and during cold Quito nights
The warmth spreads from your throat to your chest — it's a hug in a cup
drinks.description: Ecuador's highland hot cocktail — cinnamon-spiced cane sugar liquor with naranjilla juice, sipped steaming during cold Andean nights. Canelazo at festivals and markets is a viral Ecuadorian travel moment — the cold mountain air and the warm cup are the perfect contrast.
